method: angr symbolic execution: stdin modeled as symbolic bitvectors (80 register bytes symbolic, 3 control bytes concretized to the trigger len=80/size=2/op=0); BP_AFTER mem_write breakpoint checks whether stores into canary_after carry the stdin symbols
notes: CONTROL-BYTE CONCRETIZATION: the 3 control bytes are fixed to the trigger geometry (len=80, size=2, op=0) so the loop bound is concrete and angr follows the single trigger path -- the fair analog of the DBI runs (which fix these same bytes); leaving len symbolic would fork the loop and cause path explosion. The 80 register bytes are symbolic (attacker data). FINDING: the stride-4 loop performs priv->len/2=40 iterations; the last 20 (here 20) OVERSHOOT into canary_after at offsets [0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52, 56, 60, 64, 68, 72, 76] -- a real OOB write that angr observes (0 in the patched harness). BUT their stored VALUES are CONCRETE, not attacker-tainted: with sreg=dreg=0 the source pointer s[i] overshoots in lockstep with dst d[i], so for i>=20 the loop reads the (concrete) sentinel it just reached and byte-swaps it in place -- attacker/stdin data is written only IN-BOUNDS (regs offsets 0..77). Confirmed natively: canary_after output is invariant across different stdin register bytes. Hence sink_value_tainted=False and sink_addr_input_dependent=False (address is a concrete loop index). This is a precision result: angr's symbolic data-flow does not over-taint the in-place byteswap, whereas the DBI shadow (microtaint) reports these 20 writes as value-tainted. angr's discriminating vuln-vs-fixed signal here is the OOB-write OCCURRENCE (n_oob_writes 20 vs 0), not value taint.

extra.empirical_value_invariance: native harness prints identical canary_after[0..7]=cd ef ef cd cd ef ef cd for stdin register bytes 0x42/0x99/0x00 -> OOB values are input-independent (sentinel bytes byte-swapped in place)
